business_scope.primary_industry_name: Out-of-Gauge (OOG) Heavy Industrial Project Cargo Logistics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid / Bijural (Civil Law for private law matters in Quebec; Common Law for public law at the federal level)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CETA (Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union)
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership)
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2012; in force 2014)
Canada-Hong Kong Investment Agreement (2016; in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended, with SOR/2002-184 (PCMLTFR) and SOR/2001-317 (Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 (s. 462.3 et seq.); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), S.C. 2017, c. 21. Quebec: An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (arts. 3, 16-21, 38-44; mandatory beneficial-ownership statements); Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991 (arts. 2236-2267, limited partnership / société en commandite); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. Although pure freight-arranging activity is not itself a PCMLTFA reporting business, the partnership's shareholders, financing institutions and banking counterparties apply these AML/CFT obligations, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec requires UBO disclosure independently of the federal regime.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Apostille Convention jurisdictions) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each natural-person general partner and each UBO meeting the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the signatory's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Name Reservation Confirmation / Attestation de réservation de nom issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (required only where the reservation confirmation is tendered to a foreign bank or partner authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized Power of Attorney from each foreign partner appointing the Quebec attorney-in-fact for registration filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the partner's jurisdiction, certified by the competent authority of that jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (only for states not party to the Apostille Convention)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory: (i) identification and verification of every general partner, every limited partner triggering the 25% UBO threshold, and any natural person exercising control-in-fact, supported by certified-copy evidence; (ii) PEP screening of all partners, directors and UBOs under s. 9 PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance, with enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their family members and close associates; (iii) sanctions screening against Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and U.S. OFAC SDN/Non-SDN lists given the cross-border project-cargo corridor; (iv) adverse media and integrity checks, including screening against procurement debarment lists applicable to federal and provincial infrastructure freight; (v) five-year retention of KYC/UBO records and FINTRAC STR filing obligations in the event any transaction gives reasonable grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online registration and name-reservation portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and arts. 13-27 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), the registered name must be in French; a non-French version may be added only where a distinct French version appears at least as prominently in official filings, signage and commercial documents. A foreign-language name may be used without French translation only if it is a registered trademark or a distinctive sign recognized under ss. 22-25 of the Charter. The registry records names in the Latin alphabet with standard French diacritics (e.g., 'Québec'). Names originating in non-Latin scripts require a phonetic Latin transliteration together with a French version; false or misleading transliterations are prohibited. A Quebec limited partnership must include in its name a legal form element indicating limited liability, such as 'Société en commandite' / 'S.E.C.' or 'Limited Partnership' / 'L.P.'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Construction / Contractor (regulated activities requiring licensing under Quebec building and professional statutes)
Québec / Canada / Royal / National / Crown (terms carrying official or governmental connotation requiring prior written authorization or a demonstrably non-misleading factual basis)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CCQ), arts. 2209-2238 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 9-20 (declaration of registration); Partnership Agreement required under CCQ art. 2210
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Registre des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) on the prescribed form under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership. Capital contributions are determined in the partnership agreement, and no escrow account is mandated by Quebec law. A nominal initial contribution may be reflected in the declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The General Partner hereby subscribes for the sole limited partnership interest in [LP Name] on behalf of the Partnership; (2) the registered office of the Partnership is fixed at [Address], Quebec, and the Registrar of Enterprises is appointed as statutory agent for service of process; (3) the General Partner is authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; (4) [Name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer and [Name] is appointed Operations Manager, with full authority to establish bank accounts, negotiate project-cargo contracts, and execute ancillary documents; (5) all actions of the incorporator in connection herewith are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation / NUANS Preliminary Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a NUANS-style name search to ensure the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing enterprise names in Quebec. If the name is protected or desired, file a name reservation request through the Enterprise Registrar's online services. Pay the prescribed search fee and retain the confirmation slip.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or authorisation if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select a revised corporate name and refile. Alternatively, file an appeal within 30 days to the Court of Québec under art. 27 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial services / Law firm authorized in Quebec (no government filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a notarized or written limited partnership agreement specifying the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management authority, duration, and transfer restrictions. Ensure the agreement complies with CCQ arts. 2209-2238. Notarization is recommended to facilitate banking and registration.
required_dossiers: Identification of each partner (full legal name, address, date of birth for individuals or registration number for entities)
Notarized identity verification for general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a document is illegible or incomplete, the notary or lawyers correct the defect before registration. Any challenge to validity may be cured by signing an amending agreement and, if necessary, applying for rectification before the Enterprise Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Déclaration d'immatriculation (online services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration electronically via the Registraire's secure portal. Include the legal name, registered office address in Quebec, the general partner's name and Quebec establishment identification, the partnership's general object, and the mandate of the representative. Pay the registration fee online, and obtain the enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement (may be kept upon request)
General partner's incorporation documents or identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or notice of deficiency, respond within the statutory delay by completing the form or supplying missing annexes. A refusal may be contested through an application for review under ss. 43-46 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Obligations and Bank Mandate Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec; Canada Revenue Agency; Banking institution in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the enterprise number is granted, complete statutory disclosures: file any update of declarations, obtain a Quebec business number for GST/QST from Revenu Québec, and for employer requirements register with the CNESST and Revenu Québec. Open a bank account in the partnership's name and provide a certified copy of the registration certificate and partnership agreement to the financial institution.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form with authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If provincial tax registration is delayed, contact the applicable desk and file using the NEQ. For banking errors, provide updated certified documents and, if needed, obtain a resolution from the general partner clarifying signatories.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (Quebec Ministry of Transportation and Sustainable Mobility) – for special movement permits of out-of-gauge/overweight loads on highways
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permit for Special Movement (heavy and oversized vehicle permit) under the Quebec Highway Safety Code, as well as any federal/oversize permit issued by the applicable transport authority

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (Quebec Ministry of Environment, Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full environmental impact assessment (EIA). The project-cargo logistics activity involves office coordination, trucking, and temporary staging, and does not constitute an industrial facility with a mandatory environmental authorization threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core activity; however, any vehicle or generator emissions must meet the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 and Quebec air quality regulations. Fugitive waste from packaging, straps, or dunnage must be handled under the Quebec Residual Materials Regulation. No wastewater discharge threshold is triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for any warehouse/office space under the Quebec Fire Safety Act; structural load-bearing verification for staging areas exceeding 5 tonnes; and workplace occupational health clearance from CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail) for safe handling and rigging operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC) for federal GST/HST and federal income tax; Revenu Québec (RQ) for QST and Quebec provincial income tax; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs/export declarations. Federal portal: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html). Provincial portal: Revenu Québec ClicSÉUR Affaires (revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/clicseur-affaires).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Quebec limited partnership (LP) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and a Quebec establishment number; this is the provincial master identification for all subsequent Quebec tax accounts. Step 2: Obtain the federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or, for non-resident applicants, CRA Form RC391 (Election/Registration for the GST/HST for Non-Resident Registrants); the LP must be registered by its general partner, and BN program accounts (GST/HST account RT, payroll RP, corporate income RC) must be opened. Step 3: Register for the QST at Revenu Québec using Form LM-1-V (Application for Registration) or electronically through ClicSÉUR Affaires; a QST account is required where the LP is a QST registrant, and Quebec payroll and tax-deduction accounts must be set up when employees are engaged. Step 4: Establish non-resident partner compliance: non-resident corporate or individual partners must obtain Canadian tax identifiers, file Form NR6 (undertaking regarding Canadian-source income) or accept Part XIII withholding, and receive T5013A partnership slips; the LP must annually file the T5013 Partnership Information Return and issue T5013/T5013A slips where it is a limited partnership or has corporate or non-resident partners. Step 5: Apply for CBSA customs/export account identification and, where applicable, a carrier/transporter code for heavy-haul cross-border movements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act (ITA s. 96 and Income Tax Folio S4-F1-C1): income, losses and gains are computed at the partnership level but taxed in the hands of partners according to their proportionate shares. The limited partner enjoys limited liability; the LP itself is not a Canadian taxpayer for income tax purposes. However, for GST/HST and QST purposes the LP is a distinct 'person' and is separately registrable/adjudicated as a registrant supplier. For treaty purposes, Canada-US Tax Treaty Article IV(7) (fiscally transparent entities) governs partner-level benefits where a US or other non-resident partner is involved.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not maintain a US-style 'check-the-box' election regime; entity classification is determined by common law, CRA administrative guidance (Income Tax Folio S4-F1-C1) and treaty provisions. Elections commonly available to a Quebec LP include: (i) ITA s. 97(2) election for tax-deferred transfer of partnership property to a newly formed Canadian corporation (useful for EPC asset/equipment migration); (ii) ITA s. 85(1) corporate rollover elections on transfer of business assets; (iii) ITA s. 216(1) election for non-resident partners to file a Canadian return on Canadian-source rental income and s. 217 election regarding pension/employment-type income; (iv) ITA ss. 18.2/18.3 hybrid mismatch elections to neutralize deduction-without-inclusion outcomes for cross-border interest/royalty flows; (v) Pillar Two global minimum tax elections under the OECD/G20 GloBE rules implemented by Canada for fiscal years beginning after 15 December 2024 (inclusive of qualified domestic top-up tax payment elections); and (vi) GST/HST and QST elections permitting a separately reporting branch/division under ETA ss. 271/273 and Quebec equivalents. For non-resident subcontractors, a payer must also consider Regulation 105 withholding (15% on fees for services rendered in Canada) and treaty-based waiver applications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT regime: federal GST (Goods and Services Tax, ETA) at 5% plus Quebec QST (Quebec Sales Tax, Excise Tax Act-equivalent provincial VAT) at 9.975%; combined standard headline rate quoted as 14.975% (QST is computed on the GST-inclusive price, producing an effective combined burden of approximately 15.47% on the tax-exclusive invoice value). Quebec is a 'participating province' only for certain HST-related transitional rules but administers QST separately from the federal HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — small-supplier threshold common to GST/HST (Excise Tax Act s. 148) and QST (Quebec Taxation Act); registration is compulsory for an entity, including a non-resident-owned Quebec LP, where taxable supplies made in Canada in the current calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters exceed C$30,000. Registration is also mandatory without regard to the threshold for non-residents supplying specified digital services or supplies relating to Canadian real property (e.g., warehousing/terminal heavy-haul staging services situated in Quebec), and for any person electing to register voluntarily to claim input tax credits. The threshold is measured on worldwide taxable supplies for small-supplier qualification, but Canadian-source supplies determine the registration trigger.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Canada operates no real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal-invoice stamping, or mandatory CTRX/API e-invoice validation regime comparable to Mexico/Italy/Brazil. GST/HST and QST returns must be filed electronically where the registrant exceeds prescribed revenue thresholds (mandatory e-filing has been phased in for registrants with annual taxable supplies above C$1.5 million; Revenu Québec similarly requires electronic QST filing and remittance via ClicSÉUR Affaires for most registrants). Pan-Canadian Peppol BIS 3.0 electronic invoicing is available on a voluntary basis under the national e-invoicing service; CBSA provides API-based eManifest and ACE export/import filing channels for customs data but these are not fiscal-clearing controls. Digital stamping and real-time tax authority clearance do not apply in Quebec or federally.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST and QST registrant supplying 'heavy-haul out-of-gauge project cargo logistics' may zero-rate: (i) supplies of tangible personal property that is exported from Canada in accordance with ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 1 (export of goods by a registrant, excluding goods consumed or altered in Canada); (ii) transportation services to a place outside Canada (Schedule VI, Part VII, section 1) — including cross-border heavy-haul trucking/ocean freight of OOG project cargo from Canadian origin; (iii) services performed on exported goods that are delivered to non-residents and used exclusively outside Canada (Schedule VI, Part V, sections 2–4), e.g., rigging/load-securing engineering for export cargo; and (iv) supplies of goods/services to a non-resident for use otherwise than in Canada where export documentation is complete. The Quebec QST zero-rating provisions mirror the GST rules (Title II, Chapter 3, Division IV of the QST Act). Eligibility requires that the supplier retains records proving the goods were delivered to a carrier for direct export, exported promptly, and not returned to Canada; the same documentation supports the exporter's input tax credit (ITC) and refund position.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export evidence: completed Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) filing or equivalent AESDirect/CCI record for controlled or regulated OOG cargo, including the export permit where required

Transport document: full-set original or ISO-certified copy of the bill of lading, CMR waybill or intermodal rail/ocean waybill evidencing movement from the Canadian Quebec staging point to a foreign destination, with the foreign destination named and no intermediate Canadian discharge

Commercial substantiation: signed commercial invoice, packing list, transport contract/freight booking confirmation, and inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice demonstrating repatriation of foreign-currency sale proceeds into the LP's Canadian financial institution account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess export zero-rating claims retroactively (generally 4 years; extended to 8 years where gross negligence exists; unlimited in cases of fraud). Where export documentation is incomplete, contradictory, or the cargo never physically departed Canada, CRA will re-characterize the supply as taxable at 5% GST (and RQ at 9.975% QST), deny input tax credits, and recover the tax with arrears interest at prescribed rates; the gross-negligence penalty under ETA s. 285.1 (25% of the net tax amount) and parallel QST penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act apply for false statements or omissions. Criminal exposure arises under ETA ss. 327/329 and the Criminal Code for wilful evasion or fraud in export refund schemes. Although Canada imposes no hard statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, the 180-day window is the CRA's evidentiary benchmark for matching export invoices to inward remittances; unrepatriated proceeds beyond 180 days trigger heightened audit scrutiny, forensic tracing, and potential denial of zero-rating unless a documented credit-period/trade-finance rationale (e.g., standby letter of credit) is provided. Records supporting zero-rated exports must be retained for at least six years from the end of the fiscal year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); also supervised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential matters and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF compliance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility of the Canadian dollar (CAD) for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions on the repatriation of capital, dividends, profits, or loan repayments for non-resident partners. However, non-resident limited partners may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax on certain Canadian-source payments (e.g., distributions characterized as interest, rents, or management fees), unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty. No prior regulatory approval is required for capital inflows or outflows; reporting obligations exist under the Census and Statistics Act for large transactions and under the Income Tax Act for certain foreign investments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds surrender. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign accounts, subject to general record-keeping rules under the Income Tax Act and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. For project cargo logistics, standard practice is to invoice in the contract currency and settle via normal banking channels without any requirement to convert receipts into CAD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Limited. Foreign-incorporated electronic money institutions (EMIs) operating as unregulated entities in Canada must register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC if they engage in money transfers or payment services. Even when registered, EMIs generally lack direct access to the Canadian clearing and settlement infrastructure (e.g., the Large Value Transfer System, ACSS). Consequently, the reliance on an offshore EMI for project cargo logistics settlements is not recommended as a primary treasury rail. For auxiliary payments (e.g., disbursing minor invoice payments), a compliant MSB/EMI registered with FINTRAC may be viable only if it maintains a Canadian presence or a correspondent banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident limited partnership opening an account in Quebec, Canadian banks generally require general partners or authorized signatories to attend an in-person KYC interview at a branch, especially for accounts with non-resident ownership. Remote opening is permissible in limited circumstances (e.g., using third-party identification and notarized documents), but tier-1 banks typically mandate a face-to-face meeting for the general partner (or a designated agent) for the initial account establishment. Specific documentary requirements may include: original partnership agreement, certificate of registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), proof of identity of all general partners, and a resolution authorizing account signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership transparency (ownership of the LP by non-resident limited partners not fully disclosed in the public register)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of the partnership agreement; a beneficial ownership schedule identifying all partners with 25% or more of capital or income; a formal directory from the jurisdiction of formation (if an offshore entity); tax identification numbers and passport copies of general partners; an explanatory memorandum demonstrating the government-issued project contract and the underlying logistics supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds / capital injection from a tax haven or non-equivalent jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide audited financial statements of the contributing limited partner; bank reference letters from an internationally recognised financial institution; evidence of the economic substance of the contributor (e.g., payroll records, physical office lease, operating history); transaction trail of the capital transfer (wire confirmation with legal purpose codes); a notarised affidavit explaining the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business jurisdiction or sanctions screening concerns (trade counterparty exposure to sanctioned entities)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full counterparty registry with passport details of ultimate beneficial owners; export/import classification of the project cargo (HS codes and ISIC mapping); contractual certification that no goods or services originate from sanctioned countries (e.g., OFAC, UNSC, EU, and Canadian Autonomous Sanctions); an independent sanctions screening report from a legal counsel or third-party compliance vendor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Project cargo logistics and freight forwarder red flags (false invoicing, trade-based money laundering)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the underlying transportation and logistics contract (e.g., FIDIC-based or NAVLPO for heavy-lift); bill of lading and commercial invoices showing cargo weight, dimensions, route, and freight charges; evidence of customs brokerage and licences held by the partnership; a project-specific due diligence file confirming the business is a bona fide Out-of-Gauge (OOG) heavy haul operator.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For capital contributions from foreign limited partners into the Quebec LP, the appropriate clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfer (or Canadian LVT via CLS for CAD). The recommended purpose code for cross-border inflow is S010 (Investment in Equity Capital) under the International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) or, if in USD/CAD, F101 (Investment). The bank remittance instruction must include: (a) the partnership's full legal name as recorded at REQ; (b) account number; (c) a compliance reference line identifying the limited partner's identity and the capital call notice number; (d) the ISO 20022 message source with the proper purpose code; and (e) for funding of the Capital Escrow Account, an escrow disbursement schedule signed by the general partner. The bank will require a copy of the capital call letter and a certificate confirming the LP has satisfied its subscription obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails for trade settlements are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cash wire payments if counterparties accept direct bank transfers, with a reference to the underlying invoice and beneficiary bank BIC; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued through a Canadian chartered bank (e.g., RBC, BMO) for high-value milestone payments, particularly for transportation of OOG cargo where the seller's bank requires a documentary presentation; (3) Contractual milestones can be structured under a standby L/C performance guarantee or advance payment guarantee, using the ICC UCP 600 and URDG 758 rules. For CAD-denominated settlements, the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) and Real-Time Rail (RTR) are used for domestic clearing. For foreign-currency disbursements (USD, EUR, GBP), banks route via SWIFT and use correspondent banking networks; the LP may also leverage a Canadian dollar prepayment account to avoid conversion spreads.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forward contracts (CAD/USD or CAD/EUR) permitted through Canadian Schedule I banks, non-deliverable, with ISDA or bank master agreement, subject to IFRS hedge accounting if documented as a cash flow hedge.

Currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for multi-year project cash flow matching, available via CSA clearing obligations only if above the five-year benchmark thresholds; otherwise bilaterally under ISDA credit support annex.
FX options (put/call on CAD) for protecting against adverse currency movements in project bids; OTC options permitted with Canadian dealers, embedded in the Bank of Canada's market guidelines.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for CAD as the currency is fully convertible and NDF markets are informal; instead, banks quote deliverable forwards with outright settlement.
Foreign exchange swaps (swap-forward combinations) for managing temporary cash positions, subject to the bank's counterparty credit limits and the LP's treasury risk policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return including GIFI financial data schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 5 months after fiscal year-end if all partners are Canadian residents; 10 months after fiscal year-end if any partner is a non-resident (non-resident ownership is permitted for this LP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD $50 per day, minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $5,000 for fiscal years ending after 2023; knowing false statements attract gross negligence penalties under s.163 ITA; repeated non-filing may result in E-file suspension and reassessment of partners' allocated income with interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CO-17 Partnership Information Return with Relevé 19 slips to partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the federal T5013: 5 months after fiscal year-end if all partners are resident in Canada, otherwise 10 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of CAD $25 per day, minimum CAD $100, maximum CAD $2,500 under s.54.5 of the Tax Administration Act (Quebec); non-filing exposes partners to reassessment, interest and administrative demand letters

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Registration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the LP's registration with the REQ
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee increases to CAD $48; failure to file for three consecutive annual periods triggers a published notice and cancellation of the registration, after which the LP loses capacity to sue, be sued, or carry on business in Quebec until a late revival declaration is accepted (revival generally possible within 2 years of cancellation)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership solely by reason of revenue, assets, or partner count; an audit becomes compulsory if (i) the partnership agreement or lender loan covenants require audited financial statements, (ii) the corporate general partner is unable to obtain a unanimous waiver of auditor appointment under articles 165–166 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1), or (iii) banking drawdowns under milestone letter-of-credit facilities require an audited statement; the CRA and Revenu Québec retain unrestricted audit rights over the partnership's books regardless of these thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) applies only if the LP is publicly accountable; a private project-cargo LP should apply ASPE (Part II) for T5013/CO-17 GIFI reporting unless the partnership agreement mandates IFRS; books kept in Canadian dollars with foreign-exchange translation per the chosen framework; CRA statutory record retention is 6 years under s.230 ITA and equivalent Quebec rules, with the 7-year benchmark adopted here for project-contract file integrity

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual REQ declaration must re-confirm each general and limited partner's legal name, residence, and registration number, and must certify the general partner's authority; there is no separate annual UBO filing for Quebec LPs at the partnership level, but partner-level transparency is enforced through the public REQ register and the annual T5013/CO-17 allocations; if a corporate general partner exercises significant control, the corporate GP must maintain and annually confirm its register of individuals with significant control under applicable CBCA/Quebec corporate transparency rules
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (partners ledger showing general and limited partners with capital contributions and profit-sharing rights)
Register of Directors (record of general partner appointment and authorization instruments)
Minute Book (partner resolutions, consents, and general partner meeting records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $300 - $1,200 (annual Quebec registered office and corporate secretarial agent services, including REQ declaration handling and registered place of business)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $12,000 - $25,000 for a full certified audit of a project-cargo LP; a review engagement of $4,000 - $8,000 is the typical market substitute when no lender or partnership agreement mandates a full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined Federal (15%) and Quebec provincial (11.5%) general corporate rates, applied to taxable corporate partners on allocated partnership income; the LP itself is fiscally transparent
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 5229 logistics partnerships; eligible partners may claim federal investment tax credits (e.g., ITC for qualified property), Quebec's refundable tax credits for logistics/innovation, and the federal small business deduction only if the partner is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) with active business income
